records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח יְהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ־בִּן־נ֠וּן מִֽן־הַשִּׁטִּ֞ים שְׁנַֽיִם־אֲנָשִׁ֤ים מְרַגְּלִים֙ חֶ֣רֶשׁ לֵאמֹ֔ר לְכ֛וּ רְא֥וּ אֶת־הָאָ֖רֶץ וְאֶת־יְרִיח֑וֹ וַיֵּ֨לְכ֜וּ וַ֠יָּבֹאוּ בֵּית־אִשָּׁ֥ה זוֹנָ֛ה וּשְׁמָ֥הּ רָחָ֖ב וַיִּשְׁכְּבוּ־שָֽׁמָּה׃
records.gloss: And sent Joshua son of Nun from the Shittim two men spying secretly, saying, go, see the land and Jericho. And they went and came [to the] house of a woman, a prostitute, and her name [was] Rahab, and they lay down there.
pieces: Then Joshua son of Nun secretly sent two men from Shittim to spy. "Go and look over the land," he told them, "and Jericho above all." So they set off and came to the house of a prostitute named Rahab, and they stayed the night there.

L.1: And Joshua son of Nun sent two men from Shittim as spies, secretly, saying, "Go, look over the land, and Jericho." And they went and came into the house of a woman, a prostitute, and her name [was] Rahab, and they lay down there.

R.1: Joshua son of Nun was camped at Shittim. From there he sent out two men in secret to spy. He told them, "Go and look over the land, especially the city of Jericho." So the two men went. They came to the house of a prostitute named Rahab and stayed there for the night.

decisions.choice: Shittim: Israel's last camp east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Shittim ("acacia trees") is on the plains of Moab, where Israel camped before crossing (Numbers 25:1; 33:49). The camp moves from there to the Jordan in 3:1.

decisions.choice: the land, and Jericho: Jericho in particular
alternatives: the land and the city of Jericho as two separate tasks
decisions.reason: The "and" picks out the first city in their path from the land as a whole. Jericho guarded the way up from the Jordan into the hill country.

decisions.choice: a woman who was a prostitute, named Rahab
decisions.reason: The word (zonah) is the ordinary word for a woman who sells sex (Genesis 38:15; Leviticus 21:7). An old Aramaic translation of Joshua calls her an innkeeper, perhaps to soften the story, but the Hebrew word does not mean that. The New Testament keeps the plain sense: it names "Rahab the prostitute" as an example of faith that acted (Hebrews 11:31; James 2:25). A stranger's coming and going at such a house would draw less notice.

decisions.choice: they lay down there: they lodged for the night
decisions.reason: The verb means to lie down, and in a setting like this it is the ordinary word for staying the night (verse 8 says they had not yet lain down to sleep). Nothing in the story says the men used her as a prostitute.

decisions.choice: a prostitute named Rahab
alternatives: a woman, a prostitute, whose name was Rahab
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "a woman, a prostitute, and her name was Rahab"; Balanced and Readable join the three parts into one phrase, and Literal keeps them.

decisions.choice: Joshua son of Nun was camped at Shittim
decisions.reason: Readable says what Shittim was, so the reader knows where the spies started (m1).

records.heading: Rahab hides the two spies

records.source: וַיֵּ֣אָמַ֔ר לְמֶ֥לֶךְ יְרִיח֖וֹ לֵאמֹ֑ר הִנֵּ֣ה אֲ֠נָשִׁים בָּ֣אוּ הֵ֧נָּה הַלַּ֛יְלָה מִבְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לַחְפֹּ֥ר אֶת־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And it was said to [the] king of Jericho, saying, look, men have come here tonight from [the] sons of Israel to search out the land.
pieces: The king of Jericho was told, "Some men from the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} have come here tonight to search out the land."

L.2: And it was told to the king of Jericho, saying, "Look, men have come here tonight from the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel to search out the land."

R.2: Someone told the king of Jericho, "Listen! Some men from Israel came here tonight. They have come to find out about our land."

decisions.choice: the king of Jericho: the ruler of a city-state
decisions.reason: Canaan was divided among many small cities, each with its own king (12:9-24 lists thirty-one of them). Jericho's king ruled the city and the land around it.

decisions.choice: to search out the land: to explore it for an attack
decisions.reason: The verb (chafar) means to dig or search; here it is to find out the land's ways in, as in Deuteronomy 1:22.

decisions.choice: men from Israel
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the sentence short; the people are the same.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַח֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְרִיח֔וֹ אֶל־רָחָ֖ב לֵאמֹ֑ר ה֠וֹצִיאִי הָאֲנָשִׁ֨ים הַבָּאִ֤ים אֵלַ֨יִךְ֙ אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֣אוּ לְבֵיתֵ֔ךְ כִּ֛י לַחְפֹּ֥ר אֶת־כָּל־הָאָ֖רֶץ בָּֽאוּ׃
records.gloss: And sent [the] king of Jericho to Rahab, saying, bring out the men, the [ones] coming to you who came into your house, for to search out all the land they have come.
pieces: So the king of Jericho sent word to Rahab: "Bring out the visitors who came to you and went into your house. They have come to spy out the whole land."

L.3: And the king of Jericho sent to Rahab, saying, "Bring out the men who came to you, who came into your house, for they have come to search out all the land."

R.3: So the king sent a message to Rahab. It said, "Bring out the men who came to your house. They are spies. They have come to look over our whole land."

decisions.choice: who came to you, who came into your house: said twice for force
decisions.reason: The king's message names the men twice over, as if to leave Rahab no room to deny they were there.

decisions.choice: They are spies.
decisions.reason: Readable states plainly what "to search out the land" means here.

records.source: וַתִּקַּ֧ח הָֽאִשָּׁ֛ה אֶת־שְׁנֵ֥י הָאֲנָשִׁ֖ים וַֽתִּצְפְּנ֑וֹ וַתֹּ֣אמֶר׀כֵּ֗ן בָּ֤אוּ אֵלַי֙ הָֽאֲנָשִׁ֔ים וְלֹ֥א יָדַ֖עְתִּי מֵאַ֥יִן הֵֽמָּה׃
records.gloss: And took the woman the two men and hid him, and she said, so, came to me the men, and not I knew from where they [were].
pieces: But the woman had taken the two men and hidden them. "It is true, the men did come to me," she said, "but I did not know where they came from.

L.4: But the woman had taken the two men and hidden them. And she said, "Yes, the men came to me, but I did not know where they [were] from.

R.4: But Rahab had already hidden the two men. She answered, "Yes, the men came to my house. But I did not know where they were from.

decisions.choice: had taken ... and hidden them: done before the king's men arrived
alternatives: took and hid them then, while the messengers waited
decisions.reason: The verbs simply carry the story on, but she cannot hide the men in front of the king's messengers. The narrator goes back to tell what she had already done; verse 6 says how.

decisions.choice: hid them: literally "hid him"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew pronoun is singular. It may mean she hid each man in turn, or it may treat the pair as one group; the sense is that both were hidden.

decisions.choice: Rahab's answer: a deliberate deception
decisions.reason: Rahab admits what cannot be denied and lies about the rest (verse 5). The story tells it without comment; later Scripture praises her faith and her receiving the spies (Hebrews 11:31; James 2:25), not the lie as such.

decisions.choice: It is true
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word (ken, "so, right") grants the point. Balanced lets her concede it before she misleads them.

records.source: וַיְהִ֨י הַשַּׁ֜עַר לִסְגּ֗וֹר בַּחֹ֨שֶׁךְ֙ וְהָאֲנָשִׁ֣ים יָצָ֔אוּ לֹ֣א יָדַ֔עְתִּי אָ֥נָה הָלְכ֖וּ הָֽאֲנָשִׁ֑ים רִדְפ֥וּ מַהֵ֛ר אַחֲרֵיהֶ֖ם כִּ֥י תַשִּׂיגֽוּם׃
records.gloss: And it was [that] the gate [was] to shut at the darkness, and the men went out; not I know where went the men. Pursue quickly after them, for you will overtake them.
pieces: When the gate was about to be shut at dark, the men left. I do not know where they went. Go after them quickly. You will catch them."

L.5: And it was [time] for the gate to be shut at dark, and the men went out. I do not know where the men went. Pursue them quickly, for you will overtake them."

R.5: When it got dark and it was time to close the city gate, the men left. I do not know where they went. Hurry and chase them! You can still catch them."

decisions.choice: the gate was to be shut at dark
decisions.reason: A walled city closed its gate at nightfall for safety (Nehemiah 7:3). Rahab claims the men left just before it closed, so they must already be outside the city.

decisions.choice: for you will overtake them: a reason to hurry
decisions.reason: She urges speed by promising success: they are not far ahead.

records.source: וְהִ֖יא הֶעֱלָ֣תַם הַגָּ֑גָה וַֽתִּטְמְנֵם֙ בְּפִשְׁתֵּ֣י הָעֵ֔ץ הָעֲרֻכ֥וֹת לָ֖הּ עַל־הַגָּֽג׃
records.gloss: And she, she had brought them up to the roof and hid them in [the] flax of the wood, the [ones] laid out by her on the roof.
pieces: In fact she had brought them up to the roof and covered them with the flax stalks she had spread out there.

L.6: But she had brought them up to the roof and hidden them among the stalks of flax that she had laid out on the roof.

R.6: Rahab had really taken the men up to her flat roof. She had hidden them under stalks of flax that she had spread out there to dry.

decisions.choice: she had brought them up: told now, done earlier
decisions.reason: The sentence begins with "she" and breaks the run of the story, the Hebrew way of giving background. It explains the hiding of verse 4.

decisions.choice: stalks of flax laid out on the roof
decisions.reason: Roofs were flat and were used for work and sleep (1 Samuel 9:25-26). Flax was pulled in spring (Exodus 9:31) and laid out to dry before its fibers were made into linen. The season fits the crossing at the time of harvest (3:15) and Passover (5:10).

decisions.choice: flat roof ... to dry
decisions.reason: Readable adds what a reader needs to picture the scene (m2).

records.source: וְהָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים רָדְפ֤וּ אַֽחֲרֵיהֶם֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן עַ֖ל הַֽמַּעְבְּר֑וֹת וְהַשַּׁ֣עַר סָגָ֔רוּ אַחֲרֵ֕י כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר יָצְא֥וּ הָרֹדְפִ֖ים אַחֲרֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And the men pursued after them [the] way of the Jordan to the fords, and the gate they shut after as the pursuers had gone out after them.
pieces: So the men set out after them along the road to the Jordan, as far as the river crossings, and as soon as the pursuers had gone out, the gate was shut.

L.7: And the men pursued them on the road to the Jordan, as far as the fords; and they shut the gate after the pursuers had gone out after them.

R.7: So the king's men went after the spies. They took the road toward the Jordan River and went as far as the places where people cross it. As soon as they had gone out, the city gate was shut.

decisions.choice: the fords: shallow places where the Jordan could be crossed
decisions.reason: The pursuers assume the spies are heading back east to Israel's camp. The river was in flood at this season (3:15), so the fords were the only way over.

decisions.choice: the gate shut behind the pursuers
decisions.reason: The closed gate shuts the spies inside the city; their only way out is the one Rahab gives them (verse 15).

decisions.choice: river crossings (B); places where people cross it (R)
decisions.reason: "Fords" is less familiar to many readers; the meaning is the same.

records.source: וְהֵ֖מָּה טֶ֣רֶם יִשְׁכָּב֑וּן וְהִ֛יא עָלְתָ֥ה עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם עַל־הַגָּֽג׃
records.gloss: And they, before they lay down, and she went up to them on the roof,
pieces: Before the men lay down to sleep, she came up to them on the roof

L.8: And before they lay down, she came up to them on the roof,

R.8: Before the spies lay down to sleep, Rahab went up to them on the roof.

decisions.choice: before they lay down: before they settled for the night
decisions.reason: This takes up "they lay down there" from verse 1: the men had not yet gone to sleep when she came to them.

records.source: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל־הָ֣אֲנָשִׁ֔ים יָדַ֕עְתִּי כִּֽי־נָתַ֧ן יְהוָ֛ה לָכֶ֖ם אֶת־הָאָ֑רֶץ וְכִֽי־נָפְלָ֤ה אֵֽימַתְכֶם֙ עָלֵ֔ינוּ וְכִ֥י נָמֹ֛גוּ כָּל־יֹשְׁבֵ֥י הָאָ֖רֶץ מִפְּנֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: and she said to the men, I know that has given YHWH to you the land, and that has fallen dread of you on us, and that have melted all [the] inhabitants of the land before you.
pieces: and told them, "I know {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given this land to you. Terror of you has fallen on us, and everyone who lives in the land is melting in fear before you.

L.9: and she said to the men, "I know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given you the land, and that the dread of you has fallen on us, and that all the inhabitants of the land melt away before you.

R.9: She said to them, "I know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given this land to you. We are terrified of you. Everyone who lives here is weak with fear because of you.

decisions.choice: I know that the LORD has given you the land
decisions.reason: Rahab, a Canaanite, speaks of Israel's God by his name and says first what his promise has already settled (1:2-3). The spies repeat her words to Joshua (verse 24).

decisions.choice: dread has fallen ... melt away: the words of the Song of the Sea
decisions.reason: Moses' song foretold that the people of Canaan would melt away and that dread and fear would fall on them (Exodus 15:15-16; see Deuteronomy 2:25; 11:25). Rahab says it has happened.

decisions.choice: melt away: lose all courage
decisions.reason: A heart that melts is one that has lost its courage (verse 11; 5:1; Deuteronomy 20:8).

decisions.choice: melting in fear (B); weak with fear (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture and adds "in fear" so it is clear; Readable gives its sense (m3).

records.source: כִּ֣י שָׁמַ֗עְנוּ אֵ֠ת אֲשֶׁר־הוֹבִ֨ישׁ יְהוָ֜ה אֶת־מֵ֤י יַם־סוּף֙ מִפְּנֵיכֶ֔ם בְּצֵאתְכֶ֖ם מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם וַאֲשֶׁ֣ר עֲשִׂיתֶ֡ם לִשְׁנֵי֩ מַלְכֵ֨י הָאֱמֹרִ֜י אֲשֶׁ֨ר בְּעֵ֤בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּן֙ לְסִיחֹ֣ן וּלְע֔וֹג אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶחֱרַמְתֶּ֖ם אוֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: For we have heard how dried up YHWH [the] waters of [the] Sea of Reeds before you when you came out from Egypt, and what you did to [the] two kings of the Amorite[s] who [were] across the Jordan, to Sihon and to Og, whom you devoted to destruction.
pieces: We have heard how {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made the water of the Red Sea dry up before you as you left Egypt. And we have heard how you dealt with the two Amorite kings across the Jordan, Sihon and Og: you devoted them to destruction.

L.10: For we have heard how {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} dried up the waters of the Sea of Reeds before you when you came out of Egypt, and what you did to the two kings of the Amorites who [were] across the Jordan, to Sihon and to Og, whom you devoted to destruction.

R.10: We heard that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made the Red Sea dry up for you when you came out of Egypt. We also heard what you did to Sihon and Og, the two Amorite kings east of the Jordan River. You destroyed them completely, as given over to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the LORD dried up the Sea of Reeds
decisions.reason: The crossing of the sea (Exodus 14:21-22) happened forty years earlier, and the news still frightens Canaan. In 4:23 Joshua sets the crossing of the Jordan beside it.

decisions.choice: across the Jordan: here, east of it
decisions.reason: The phrase names the far side of the river from where the speaker stands. Rahab is in Jericho, west of the Jordan, so she means the land east of it, where Sihon and Og ruled.

decisions.choice: Sihon and Og, the two kings of the Amorites
decisions.reason: Israel defeated Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan and took their lands (Numbers 21:21-35; Deuteronomy 2:26-3:11).

decisions.choice: devoted to destruction: given over to God completely
decisions.reason: The verb is the one for a "devoted thing" (Leviticus 27:28-29). In war it means a people was destroyed and none were kept for gain, as with Sihon and Og (Deuteronomy 2:34; 3:6).

decisions.choice: the Red Sea
decisions.reason: The Hebrew name is "Sea of Reeds", which Literal keeps. Balanced and Readable use the familiar name for the sea Israel crossed, as Exodus does.

decisions.choice: destroyed them completely, as given over to the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable explains the term as in Deuteronomy 2:34 (m4).

records.source: וַנִּשְׁמַע֙ וַיִּמַּ֣ס לְבָבֵ֔נוּ וְלֹא־קָ֨מָה ע֥וֹד ר֛וּחַ בְּאִ֖ישׁ מִפְּנֵיכֶ֑ם כִּ֚י יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֔ם ה֤וּא אֱלֹהִים֙ בַּשָּׁמַ֣יִם מִמַּ֔עַל וְעַל־הָאָ֖רֶץ מִתָּֽחַת׃
records.gloss: And we heard, and melted our heart, and not rose again spirit in [any] man because of you, for YHWH your God, he [is] God in the heavens above and on the earth beneath.
pieces: When we heard it, our hearts melted, and no one had any courage left because of you, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is God in heaven above and on earth below.

L.11: And we heard, and our heart melted, and there did not rise up any more spirit in anyone because of you; for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} [is] God in the heavens above and on the earth beneath.

R.11: When we heard these things, we were filled with fear. No one has any courage left to fight you, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is God of the heavens above and of the earth below.

decisions.choice: no spirit rose up in anyone: no one had courage left
decisions.reason: "Spirit" (ruach) here is a person's breath and vigor; when it does not rise, a person has no will to stand and fight (5:1; 1 Kings 10:5).

decisions.choice: the LORD your God is God in heaven above and on earth beneath
decisions.reason: Rahab's confession uses the words Moses gave Israel to confess (Deuteronomy 4:39). She owns the LORD not as one god among the gods of the nations but as God of all places.

decisions.choice: our hearts melted (B); we were filled with fear (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the Hebrew picture; Readable gives its sense, since the next clause speaks of courage (m1).

decisions.choice: your God is God
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats the subject ("he") for emphasis; Literal keeps it, and Balanced and Readable carry the stress in the sentence itself.

decisions.choice: to fight you
decisions.reason: Readable says what the courage would have been for.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֗ה הִשָּֽׁבְעוּ־נָ֥א לִי֙ בַּֽיהוָ֔ה כִּי־עָשִׂ֥יתִי עִמָּכֶ֖ם חָ֑סֶד וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֨ם גַּם־אַתֶּ֜ם עִם־בֵּ֤ית אָבִי֙ חֶ֔סֶד וּנְתַתֶּ֥ם לִ֖י א֥וֹת אֱמֶֽת׃
records.gloss: And now, swear, please, to me by YHWH, since I have done with you steadfast love, that will do also you with [the] house of my father steadfast love, and give to me a sign of truth,
pieces: So now, swear to me by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: since I have shown you faithful love, you too will show faithful love to my father's family. Give me a sign I can trust

L.12: And now, please swear to me by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, since I have shown you steadfast love, that you also will show steadfast love to my father's house, and give me a sure sign,

R.12: I have shown you faithful love. So now, make a promise to me in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Promise that you will show faithful love to my family too. Give me a sign that I can trust.

decisions.choice: steadfast love: loyal kindness that keeps faith
decisions.reason: Chesed is goodness shown out of loyalty, the faithfulness one party owes another in a bond. Rahab has acted as the spies' loyal friend, and she asks that the same be done for her family. The word is used of the LORD's covenant love (Exodus 34:6; Deuteronomy 7:9).

decisions.choice: swear to me by the LORD: an oath that calls God to witness
decisions.reason: To swear by the LORD bound the spies before their own God, the one Rahab has just confessed (verse 11). Israel was to swear by his name alone (Deuteronomy 6:13).

decisions.choice: a sign of truth: a sure pledge
alternatives: a token that can be relied on
decisions.reason: "Truth" (emet) here is reliability: something she can hold them to. The oath itself (verse 14) and the scarlet cord (verse 18) give her that assurance.

decisions.choice: steadfast love (Literal); faithful love (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 34:6 and Deuteronomy, so that the loyalty in the word is kept; "kindness" alone would leave it out.

decisions.choice: my father's family (B); my family (R)
decisions.reason: "House" means the household, the family under its head; verse 13 lists who is meant.

records.source: וְהַחֲיִתֶ֞ם אֶת־אָבִ֣י וְאֶת־אִמִּ֗י וְאֶת־אַחַי֙ וְאֶת־אַחְיוֹתַ֔י וְאֵ֖ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר לָהֶ֑ם וְהִצַּלְתֶּ֥ם אֶת־נַפְשֹׁתֵ֖ינוּ מִמָּֽוֶת׃
records.gloss: and you will keep alive my father and my mother and my brothers and my sisters and all that [is] to them, and deliver our lives from death.
pieces: that you will keep my father and mother alive, with my brothers and sisters and all their people, and rescue us from death."

L.13: and that you will spare my father and my mother and my brothers and my sisters and all who belong to them, and deliver our lives from death."

R.13: Promise that you will let my father and mother live, and my brothers and sisters, and all their families. Save us from being killed."

decisions.choice: all who belong to them: their households
decisions.reason: The phrase can take in goods as well as people, but the point is life and death, so their wives, children and dependants are meant (6:23).

decisions.choice: our lives: literally "our souls"
decisions.reason: The word (nefesh) means the living person. To deliver someone's nefesh from death is to keep that person alive.

decisions.choice: all their families
decisions.reason: Readable names the people meant (m1).

records.source: וַיֹּ֧אמְרוּ לָ֣הּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים נַפְשֵׁ֤נוּ תַחְתֵּיכֶם֙ לָמ֔וּת אִ֚ם לֹ֣א תַגִּ֔ידוּ אֶת־דְּבָרֵ֖נוּ זֶ֑ה וְהָיָ֗ה בְּתֵת־יְהוָ֥ה לָ֨נוּ֙ אֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ וְעָשִׂ֥ינוּ עִמָּ֖ךְ חֶ֥סֶד וֶאֱמֶֽת׃
records.gloss: And said to her the men, our life in place of you[rs] to die, if not you tell this business of ours; and it will be, when gives YHWH to us the land, and we will do with you steadfast love and truth.
pieces: The men answered her, "We stake our lives on yours, even to death, so long as you do not tell anyone about our mission. When {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gives us the land, we will treat you with faithful love and keep our word."

L.14: And the men said to her, "Our life for yours, to death, if you do not tell this business of ours! And when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gives us the land, we will deal with you in steadfast love and faithfulness."

R.14: The men answered, "If anything happens to you, may we die in your place! But you must not tell anyone what we are doing. When {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gives us this land, we will show you faithful love and keep our promise."

decisions.choice: our life for yours, to death: the spies pledge their own lives
alternatives: our lives will be forfeit if you die
decisions.reason: It is a form of oath: if harm comes to Rahab's family through Israel, the spies' own lives are owed in exchange (compare 1 Kings 20:39, 42).

decisions.choice: this business of ours: the spies' mission
decisions.reason: The word (davar) is "word" or "matter". She must not report their errand to the king, or the oath no longer binds them (verse 20).

decisions.choice: steadfast love and faithfulness: loyalty that will be carried out
decisions.reason: The pair (chesed and emet) is used of the LORD's own covenant faithfulness (Exodus 34:6) and of a promise that will truly be kept (Genesis 24:49; 47:29). The spies answer Rahab's request (verse 12) with her own word and promise that it will be kept.

decisions.choice: steadfast love (Literal); faithful love (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 34:6 and Deuteronomy, so that the loyalty in the word is kept; "kindness" alone would leave it out.

decisions.choice: keep our word (B); keep our promise (R)
decisions.reason: Emet here is the reliability of the oath; Balanced and Readable say it as a promise kept (m3).

records.source: וַתּוֹרִדֵ֥ם בַּחֶ֖בֶל בְּעַ֣ד הַֽחַלּ֑וֹן כִּ֤י בֵיתָהּ֙ בְּקִ֣יר הַֽחוֹמָ֔ה וּבַֽחוֹמָ֖ה הִ֥יא יוֹשָֽׁבֶת׃
records.gloss: And she let them down by the rope through the window, for her house [was] in [the] side of the wall, and in the wall she [was] living.
pieces: Then she let them down by a rope through the window, because her house was built into the city wall; she lived in the wall itself.

L.15: Then she let them down by a rope through the window, for her house [was] in the side of the city wall, and she lived in the wall.

R.15: Rahab's house was built into the city wall. So she used a rope to let the men down through her window to the outside.

decisions.choice: her house was in the wall
decisions.reason: Houses could be built into or against a city's wall, so a window in the back wall opened outside the city. With the gate shut (verse 7), that window was the spies' way out. David escaped from his house the same way (1 Samuel 19:12).

decisions.choice: she let them down: the event told ahead of the talk that follows
alternatives: she spoke to them from the window after letting them down
decisions.reason: Verses 16-21 report what was said, and they speak of "the window through which you let us down" (verse 18). The narrator may tell the escape first and then go back to the words spoken before it, or the conversation may have been called down from the window.

decisions.choice: the reason first, then the escape
decisions.reason: Readable puts the house in the wall first so that the escape makes sense as it is read.

records.source: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ הָהָ֣רָה לֵּ֔כוּ פֶּֽן־יִפְגְּע֥וּ בָכֶ֖ם הָרֹדְפִ֑ים וְנַחְבֵּתֶ֨ם שָׁ֜מָּה שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֗ים עַ֚ד שׁ֣וֹב הָרֹֽדְפִ֔ים וְאַחַ֖ר תֵּלְכ֥וּ לְדַרְכְּכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And she said to them, to the hill country go, lest meet you the pursuers, and hide yourselves there three days until [the] returning of the pursuers, and after [that] you will go on your way.
pieces: She told them, "Go to the hills, so that the men chasing you will not find you. Hide there for three days until they come back, and after that you can go on your way."

L.16: And she said to them, "Go to the hill country, so that the pursuers do not meet you, and hide there three days until the pursuers return; and afterward you may go on your way."

R.16: She told them, "Go up into the hills, so that the men looking for you do not find you. Hide there for three days, until they come back. Then you can go on your way."

decisions.choice: the hill country: the hills west of Jericho
decisions.reason: The pursuers had gone east toward the Jordan (verse 7). The rough hills rising west of Jericho, the other way, had many places to hide.

decisions.choice: three days: long enough for the search to end
decisions.reason: By then the pursuers would give up and return (verse 22). The phrase may count parts of days, as in 1:11 and 3:2.

records.source: וַיֹּאמְר֥וּ אֵלֶ֖יהָ הָאֲנָשִׁ֑ים נְקִיִּ֣ם אֲנַ֔חְנוּ מִשְּׁבֻעָתֵ֥ךְ הַזֶּ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִשְׁבַּעְתָּֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: And said to her the men, free [will be] we from this oath of yours that you made us swear;
pieces: The men told her, "This oath you have made us swear will not bind us

L.17: And the men said to her, "We [will be] free from this oath of yours that you made us swear,

R.17: The men said to her, "We will be free from the promise you made us give you unless you do these things.

decisions.choice: free from your oath: released from it unless its terms are kept
decisions.reason: The word (naqi) means clean, clear of guilt or duty. The spies set out conditions in verses 18-20; if Rahab does not keep them, the oath will not bind them.

decisions.choice: the sentence runs on into verse 18
decisions.reason: "We will be free" depends on what follows: the conditions about the cord and the house.

decisions.choice: unless you do these things
decisions.reason: Readable says at once that conditions follow, since the oath's terms come only in the next verses.

records.source: הִנֵּ֛ה אֲנַ֥חְנוּ בָאִ֖ים בָּאָ֑רֶץ אֶת־תִּקְוַ֡ת חוּט֩ הַשָּׁנִ֨י הַזֶּ֜ה תִּקְשְׁרִ֗י בַּֽחַלּוֹן֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הוֹרַדְתֵּ֣נוּ ב֔וֹ וְאֶת־אָבִ֨יךְ וְאֶת־אִמֵּ֜ךְ וְאֶת־אַחַ֗יִךְ וְאֵת֙ כָּל־בֵּ֣ית אָבִ֔יךְ תַּאַסְפִ֥י אֵלַ֖יִךְ הַבָּֽיְתָה׃
records.gloss: look, we [are] coming into the land; this cord of thread of scarlet you will tie in the window that you let us down by it, and your father and your mother and your brothers and all [the] house of your father you will gather to yourself into the house.
pieces: unless, when we come into the land, you tie this scarlet cord in the window you let us down through, and bring your father and mother, your brothers and all your father's family into your house with you.

L.18: look, when we come into the land, you shall tie this cord of scarlet thread in the window through which you let us down, and you shall gather to yourself into the house your father and your mother and your brothers and all your father's house.

R.18: When we come into the land, tie this red rope in the window you let us down through. Bring your father and mother, your brothers and all your family into your house with you.

decisions.choice: look, we are coming: when we come
decisions.reason: "Look" (hinneh) points to what is about to happen. The spies set the terms that will hold on the day of attack.

decisions.choice: a cord of scarlet thread: a sign that marks the house
decisions.reason: Scarlet thread was dyed bright red and was costly (Exodus 25:4; Genesis 38:28). Hanging from the window in the wall, it would show the attackers which house to spare.

decisions.choice: cord: a word that elsewhere also means "hope"
decisions.reason: The word for this cord (tiqvah) is the same as the common word for hope, and is found meaning "cord" only here and in verse 21. Whether a play on the two senses is meant is uncertain.

decisions.choice: gathered into the marked house: the pattern of Passover
decisions.reason: As at the first Passover, a family is saved by staying inside a house marked with red while judgment falls outside, and anyone who goes out of its door is not protected (verse 19; Exodus 12:7, 13, 22). The text does not draw the link itself.

decisions.choice: unless
decisions.reason: In Balanced the conditions finish the sentence begun in verse 17: the oath does not bind them unless she does these things.

decisions.choice: red rope
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words for color and cord.

records.source: וְהָיָ֡ה כֹּ֣ל אֲשֶׁר־יֵצֵא֩ מִדַּלְתֵ֨י בֵיתֵ֧ךְ׀הַח֛וּצָה דָּמ֥וֹ בְרֹאשׁ֖וֹ וַאֲנַ֣חְנוּ נְקִיִּ֑ם וְ֠כֹל אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִֽהְיֶ֤ה אִתָּךְ֙ בַּבַּ֔יִת דָּמ֣וֹ בְרֹאשֵׁ֔נוּ אִם־יָ֖ד תִּֽהְיֶה־בּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And it will be [that] every [one] who goes out from [the] doors of your house to the outside, his blood [will be] on his head, and we [will be] free; and every [one] who will be with you in the house, his blood [will be] on our head, if a hand will be on him.
pieces: Anyone who goes out through the doors of your house into the street will be responsible for their own death, and we will be free of blame. But if anyone who is with you in the house is harmed, the blame for their death will be on us.

L.19: And it will be [that] anyone who goes out of the doors of your house into the street, his blood [will be] on his own head, and we [will be] free; but anyone who is with you in the house, his blood [will be] on our head, if a hand is laid on him.

R.19: If anyone goes out of your house into the street and is killed, it will be their own fault. We will not be to blame. But if anyone inside the house with you is hurt, we will be to blame.

decisions.choice: his blood on his head: he bears the guilt for his own death
decisions.reason: Blood that is "on someone's head" is guilt for a death laid on that person (2 Samuel 1:16; 1 Kings 2:37). Whoever leaves the house has no claim on the oath; whoever stays in it is the spies' responsibility.

decisions.choice: if a hand is on him: if anyone harms him
decisions.reason: To lay a hand on someone is to attack or harm that person (Genesis 37:22, 27).

decisions.choice: free: clear of guilt
decisions.reason: The same word as "free" from the oath (verse 17): the spies will owe nothing for that death.

decisions.choice: responsible for their own death (B); their own fault (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom (m1); Literal keeps it. "Their" refers to "anyone", man or woman.

records.source: וְאִם־תַּגִּ֖ידִי אֶת־דְּבָרֵ֣נוּ זֶ֑ה וְהָיִ֣ינוּ נְקִיִּ֔ם מִשְּׁבֻעָתֵ֖ךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִשְׁבַּעְתָּֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: And if you tell this business of ours, and we will be free from your oath that you made us swear.
pieces: And if you tell anyone about our mission, we will not be bound by the oath you made us swear."

L.20: But if you tell this business of ours, then we will be free from your oath that you made us swear."

R.20: And if you tell anyone what we are doing, we will not have to keep our promise to you."

decisions.choice: the third condition: silence
decisions.reason: This repeats the condition of verse 14. The three terms are the cord in the window, the family inside, and no word to the king.

records.source: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ כְּדִבְרֵיכֶ֣ם כֶּן־ה֔וּא וַֽתְּשַׁלְּחֵ֖ם וַיֵּלֵ֑כוּ וַתִּקְשֹׁ֛ר אֶת־תִּקְוַ֥ת הַשָּׁנִ֖י בַּחַלּֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And she said, according to your words, so it [is]. And she sent them away, and they went; and she tied the cord of the scarlet in the window.
pieces: "Agreed," she replied. "Let it be as you say." She sent them on their way, and they left. Then she tied the scarlet cord in the window.

L.21: And she said, "According to your words, so be it." And she sent them away, and they went; and she tied the scarlet cord in the window.

R.21: Rahab said, "I agree to what you say." Then she sent them away, and they left. And she tied the red rope in her window.

decisions.choice: she tied the scarlet cord: at once, or told here to finish the scene
alternatives: she tied it later, when Israel came
decisions.reason: The spies told her to tie it "when we come into the land" (verse 18). She may have done it at once, to be ready, or the narrator may tell it here to close the scene. Either way the cord is in place when Jericho falls (6:22-25).

decisions.choice: red rope
decisions.reason: As in verse 18.

records.source: וַיֵּלְכוּ֙ וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ הָהָ֔רָה וַיֵּ֤שְׁבוּ שָׁם֙ שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֔ים עַד־שָׁ֖בוּ הָרֹדְפִ֑ים וַיְבַקְשׁ֧וּ הָרֹדְפִ֛ים בְּכָל־הַדֶּ֖רֶךְ וְלֹ֥א מָצָֽאוּ׃
records.gloss: And they went and came to the hill country and stayed there three days until returned the pursuers; and sought the pursuers in all the way and not they found.
pieces: So they went into the hills and stayed there three days, until the men chasing them had gone back. The pursuers had searched all along the road without finding them.

L.22: And they went and came to the hill country and stayed there three days, until the pursuers returned; and the pursuers searched all along the road and did not find [them].

R.22: The spies went into the hills and hid there for three days. The king's men searched for them all along the road but did not find them. Then the king's men went back to the city.

decisions.choice: the pursuers searched ... and did not find them
decisions.reason: The search happened while the spies hid, before the pursuers turned back; Rahab's plan (verse 16) worked.

decisions.choice: the search told before the return
decisions.reason: Readable tells the events in the order they happened, and says where the pursuers returned to.

records.source: וַיָּשֻׁ֜בוּ שְׁנֵ֤י הָֽאֲנָשִׁים֙ וַיֵּרְד֣וּ מֵֽהָהָ֔ר וַיַּעַבְרוּ֙ וַיָּבֹ֔אוּ אֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ בִּן־נ֑וּן וַיְסַ֨פְּרוּ־ל֔וֹ אֵ֥ת כָּל־הַמֹּצְא֖וֹת אוֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: And returned [the] two men and went down from the hill country and crossed over and came to Joshua son of Nun, and recounted to him all the [things] finding them.
pieces: Then the two men came back down from the hills, crossed the river and came to Joshua son of Nun. They told him everything that had happened to them.

L.23: Then the two men returned and came down from the hill country and crossed over, and they came to Joshua son of Nun and told him all that had happened to them.

R.23: Then the two men came down out of the hills. They crossed the Jordan River and went back to Joshua son of Nun. They told him everything that had happened.

decisions.choice: crossed over: the Jordan
decisions.reason: The river is not named, but they had to cross the Jordan to reach the camp at Shittim (verse 1).

decisions.choice: all that had happened to them: literally "all the things that found them"
decisions.reason: The verb (matsa', "find") is used of events that come upon someone (Genesis 44:34; Numbers 20:14).

decisions.choice: the river (B); the Jordan River (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what they crossed (m1).

records.source: וַיֹּאמְרוּ֙ אֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ כִּֽי־נָתַ֧ן יְהוָ֛ה בְּיָדֵ֖נוּ אֶת־כָּל־הָאָ֑רֶץ וְגַם־נָמֹ֛גוּ כָּל־יֹשְׁבֵ֥י הָאָ֖רֶץ מִפָּנֵֽינוּ׃ס
records.gloss: And they said to Joshua, surely has given YHWH into our hand all the land, and also have melted all [the] inhabitants of the land before us.
pieces: "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has surely handed the whole land over to us," they told Joshua. "Everyone who lives there is melting in fear because of us."

L.24: And they said to Joshua, "Truly {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given all the land into our hand; and also all the inhabitants of the land melt away before us."

R.24: They said to Joshua, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has really given us the whole land! All the people who live there are weak with fear because of us."

decisions.choice: given into our hand: put in our power
decisions.reason: To give into someone's hand is to give victory over a place or people (6:2; 8:1; 10:8).

decisions.choice: the spies' report echoes Rahab
decisions.reason: Their words take up hers almost exactly (verse 9). Unlike the spies of Numbers 13-14, whose report made the people afraid, these men bring back courage, and it comes from a Canaanite's confession.

decisions.choice: melting in fear (B); weak with fear (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 9.
